notes.title: Starni Games returns as a publisher for the Strategic Mind series and announces
notes.content:
[h2]Greetings, Generals![/h2]

[i]It has been a rough couple of years for our team, since Russia invaded Ukraine back in February 2022. Still, our team managed to continue our work in our Kyiv office, and despite all odds delivered Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty, Headquarters: World War II, and Ukraine War Stories. [/i]

We also tried to expand the Strategic Mind series audience by making a publishing agreement with the Hyperstrange team, who later delegated their obligations to the Untold Tales team. Later, we decided to revert to[i] self-publishing for the Strategic Mind series[/i] on PC. Just a few days ago we finally got back under our direct control all of the Strategic Mind games. 

Up until now, we were limited in our communication, as we did not want to interfere with the publisher’s efforts. Now, we are free to communicate about the Strategic Mind series and we want to renew active communication with you. [i]We are really excited to finally be back![/i]

So, you can expect more events and announcements about teh Strategic Mind series in the future. 

On top of this, we have another big announcement today. Since Ukraine War Stories development, we wanted to continue the line of interactive text-based games, and today we are ready to announce our new project - [b][i]Robot’s Fate: Alice, a text-based RPG set in the future where robots with neural network AI are integral to human life. [/i]
[/b]

[previewyoutube=QxygnE6X2RA;full][/previewyoutube]

It is very different from our other titles in many ways, but it shares the immersive storytelling and narrative elements that we see as vital for our games. If you are not scared by a lot of text, give it a try, as we will be releasing a [b]free demo very soon - on August 19th.[/b] Make sure to add Robot’s Fate: Alice to your wishlist to not miss the Demo release.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3091030

Have a great weekend!

With Best Regards from Kyiv,
Oleksandr Sienin and the Starni Games team

notes.title: NEW MAJOR UPDATE - 4.00 Update is Here!
notes.content:
[h1]MAJOR UPDATE Update 4.00[/h1]

[h2]Hello, guys![/h2]

This is an update dedicated to the Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty release later today. It includes all the fixes and improvements we did to the core mechanics while working on Strategic Mind. This is just one in a series of updates aimed at polish and post-launch support of the entire series.

Today, we addressed one of the series issues that was especially noticeable if you own all Strategic Mind titles - we reduced the disk space required for all games in the series. So, now it is easier to store them. 

[h2]Update 4.00[/h2]

[list]
[*] The game now requires significantly less disk space (Before 42.3 GB | Now 27.2 GB) 
[*] Fixed various bugs while working on Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty
[*] Fixed some localization errors
[*] More fixes to come soon
[/list]


[h2]Non-exhaustive list of fixed issues:[/h2]

[list]
[*] Bug with “flying” Recon unit
[*] 3rd equipment slot abuse for some units. 
[*] The torpedo sound could still be heard when the volume is at 0.
[*] Units not getting extra EXP for capturing enemies that could not retreat due to various reasons. 
[*] Units keeping bonus from aura effects, even if the UNDO button returned the aura-giving unit away from them
[*] Abuse that allowed to return units to Reserve outside of the Deployment area.
[*] The crash caused by the illegitimate equipping of units outside the Service Zone (Which was possible due to a UI bug). 
[/list]

[h2]All other Strategic Mind titles are also receiving a similar update today. [/h2]

[b]You can expect more updates and quality-of-life improvements as we keep polishing the series and provide post-launch support for Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty and other titles[/b]. All relevant improvements will be delivered across all titles of the Strategic Mind series, as always. 

As today, with the beginning of the Steam Strategy Fest, we celebrate the release of [b]Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty[/b], you can take advantage of the special offer - all owners of the previous Strategic Mind series games can get the newest title with 15% extra discount on top of the existing launch discount. Act now, commander!

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/34460/

With best regards
Starni Games team

notes.title: Games Gathering Kyiv 2021 Conference
notes.content:
Hello, guys!

On December 4-5th our team went to one of the biggest annual Games Conferences in Eastern Europe, which was conveniently held in our hometown - Kyiv. We bought tickets for all team members who wanted to come - that means everyone really. Fortunately, we also got a few tickets for free as speakers and Indie Blast participants.  

It was a truly massive event for Game industry specialists with some 2800 people attending offline and extra 600 online. It was a great opportunity to talk to colleagues, discuss all the latest news, share experiences and just chill with like-minded people. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/e6daaea3e40a93abee163a18755edb272c68c374.jpg[/img]
Large conference hall

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/eb6268f0867942038b7f315abd90825210ac982c.jpg[/img]
Wargaming brought the real T-34-85 tank to their booth and made a lottery winning which granted a free ride in the T-34-85 tank. Quite thematic I would say. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/fd9b537b0fa32e940734d3e3c2209c848fef286c.jpg[/img]
The insides of the T-34-58 tank. Although refitted with these fancy modern LEDs to increase combat capabilities, this new equipment provides +99 style and -50 spotting. 

[h1]Indie Blast[/h1]
Now, closer to our team’s involvement in the event. It is our good tradition to present our Strategic Mind titles in the Indie Blast competition that allows us to have a small booth sponsored by Epic Games for developers working on Unreal Engine 4. So, this time was no different and we presented our upcoming title - Strategic Mind: Spirit of Liberty. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/231aade8f29ade12633b933a0d0beacf66fe83ae.jpg[/img]
Starni Games booth at the event

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/cfce3cb65fbfc2ec98fe2638e5f50b8b52d501f7.jpg[/img]
Starni team - everyone hides from the camera (they seem to have a very high camouflage parameter and are shown as "?")

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/ffa90a7205be799872da2bf4effbdc107b25708e.jpg[/img]
Visitors trying out the game. They obviously failed - one cannot just play our game at a conference successfully. It requires some more time to really get into it. :)

[h1]Starni team at Games Gathering[/h1]
This time we set a record of all 14-people-team attendance. Here are some photos that were taken by our team during the event:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/fcf31c2e96c20ef6e7412fcc8b0fb686ffff6c35.jpg[/img]
Kate Bovkun - the one and only 2D artist in our team :) Now she has finally found herself a teammate ;)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/7f36552429132bcb825623f436e9c204fc58129a.jpg[/img]
Alex Marchenko - our Lead Level Designer, ... at least that is what it says on the badge. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/0070da4fdd3fa9096bd1dd46f71f2c347cb93d7a.jpg[/img]
Valentine Kolesnikov - our Level Design Guru (also known for the best memes), even the famous David Mullich himself has asked to take a photo with Valentine. ;) (not really)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/3195cf424383255ae022c32f0b2907ad504523db.jpg[/img]
Kate Bovkun and Alexander Shevchuk are enjoying themselves at the luxurious booth of some big gaming company that makes Hidden Object games. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/5e5bbf8b3ee2ab082a865b25c75c30271d3fd076.jpg[/img]
Valentine Kolesnikov and Alex Marchenko taking some photos together to strengthen team spirit. No, just kidding - they made those photos to get free lollipops.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/23530f18d9a48fbd0abfb0130f5b0d51be6338ae.jpg[/img]
Our marketing and community manager Katya Globa is taking photos with her sister, oops it's not her sister, it is Lerika Mallayeva the CEO & Founder of DevGAMM events (big game dev conferences similar to this one).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/87205c4df40465c252809cce0d646b7699d65dcd.jpg[/img]
Aaaand finally, Alex Marchenko is taking photos with his new buddy David Mullich and talking about the development of Heroes of Might and Magic VIII. (not really)

[h1]Publisher vs Developer talk[/h1]
Our CEO Ihor Tymoshenko and COO Oleksandr Sienin had a 1-hour talk about Developer-Publisher relations: how to look for the right publisher, what things to have in mind during the negotiations, and other such things. The key takeaway would be that you have to look for a very specific publisher that fits your company and project the best and the one you can build a long-term relationship with mutual trust and respect. You should be partners, not “the boss and the subordinate”.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/807cc8cd44bac33139c4deae68a615a01b205029.jpg[/img]
Left to right: Ihor Tymoshenko and Oleksandr Sienin just started with the talk. Must be really hard to give a talk with your mouth closed. ;)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/6a7170600ad8dacc2765fd99eadf149385b5a455.jpg[/img]
The talk has not progressed much since the photo above, as could be seen from the slides. 

[h1]An unexpected guest[/h1]
One of the most famous guests of the conference was undoubtedly David Mullich - the Producer of the Heroes of Might and Magic series (HoMM 3 and HoMM 4), Vampires the Masquerade Bloodlines, and many other famous titles. It was a pleasant surprise when David came to our small booth as he was visiting the Indie zone. We told him about the Strategic Mind series, and he said that really liked how the cinematic trailer for the Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom was directed (footage cut and overall visuals) - it was shown on the screen at our booth as we spoke. We could not miss the chance and took a couple of photos with David. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/864a0dc02864d862e81c0091a9eaf10b4c4e0449.jpg[/img]
David Mullich and Oleksandr Sienin at Starni Games booth. Yay!

The next day David Mullich taught a lecture about the development of the HoMM series and his path in game development. It was very interesting since the guys on the team could really sympathize and reflect on many things he spoke about - since we often face the same problems.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/9324d646bdb63771659cbbe214080a20c7e87082.jpg[/img]
One of the slides from the David Mullich talk at the event explains the UI visual style that the HoMM3 dev team has very fittingly dubbed "the fecal brush". Did not stop them from creating an immortal game though. :)

[h1]Our new project[/h1]
Interesting thing was that since the conference was before the 14th December - when Slitherine had officially announced our new joint project Headquarters: World War II - we could not really talk about it, and kept talking about “some unannounced project". Fortunately, now the announcement has come and we finally can talk about it more or less freely. We invite you to check out the store page for and wishlist + follow to keep an eye on the development. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1840800/Headquarters_World_War_II/

Have a good day!
Starni Games team

notes.title: Community Survey: What is Your Favourite Element of Strategic Mind Games?
notes.content:
As developers we cannot help but feel attached to virtually all aspects of our games. Yet we are curious which of them are the most relevant for the players. So, we decided to ask the community what are the most important elements of the game for you. Please, help us out by sharing your thoughts on the subject - that would be a great help.

Below you can find the list of key aspects of the game in our view. They are presented in a randomly generated order to avoid bias. Please choose up to 8 key elements and put them by the order of significance:
1 = [b]8 points[/b] = most significant
2 = [b]7 points[/b] = very significant
...
8 = [b]1 point[/b] = less significant
9-17 = [b]0 points[/b] = not very significant.
Please, explain your reasoning if you can. You can also add your own points under the list in case we have missed anything. 

We hope that your answers will help us promote the series more effectively and increase the players community. That in turn will help ensure longevity and further improvement of the series, so your support is very important for us. 

[h3]Example of how your answer could be structured:[/h3]
1. 10) Both historical (75%) and alternate history (25%) operations.
Because I love history but without alternate scenarios it is a bit dull.
2. 15) Advanced naval combat system.
Since I enjoy naval combat, this system is really different from any other game.
3. 3) Lots of unit classes.
I enjoy combined arms operations and the tactical flexibility/diversity it allows.
4. 7) Different victory types, awards and ranks.
I dislike games that do not give me a sense of achievement. I also like that the achievements are meaningful in the Strategic Mind. 
5. 4) (hi)story-driven gameplay.
I like that I also learn something new about history while playing, and often it is really interesting. 
6. 17) All units gain experience and can learn additional skills every time they level up.
I like that my army is getting more powerful and experienced as the campaign progresses.
7. 9) Advanced supply system - great depth with little micromanagement.
I think it is something many games miss - a proper supply system.
8. 13) All types of units can get special equipment.
Once again the more customization and control I have over my units - the better. 

[h1]The list of features to choose from:[/h1]
[b]1)[/b] All unit models are historical and become available at historically accurate time of the campaign. Same with the enemy troops. 
[b]Example:[/b] Historically Finland had very limited military equipment and was purchasing it from different countries, so you will get to create your own mismash of historically available units: Command the Finnish Infantry and Bofors AT guns, Swedish Recon cars, captured Soviet vehicles, including BT-7, T-34, and KV tanks. Make use of pre-war British Bristol Blenheim bombers, covered by Dutch Fokker and US Buffalo fighter planes. Purchase German Pz-IV tanks, StuG assault guns, and Ju-88 bombers.

[b]2)[/b] Between the battles you can learn Headquarters skills that allow you to get unique tactical advantages. Command points system allows the flexible balance of the number of deployed troops - the more you deploy the less active HQ skills you can use. 
[b]Example:[/b] Your artillery could fire twice per turn, or your Aircraft units could land and take off without losing movement points. 

[b]3)[/b] Lots of unit classes: Infantry, Tanks, Artillery, Anti-tank guns, Anti-aircraft guns, Assault guns, Armoured trains, Reconnaissance cars, Fighters, Tactical bombers, Strategic bombers, Submarines, Destroyers, Heavy cruisers, Battleships, and Carriers. All units have their unique skills and set of level-up abilities and equipment. 
[b]Example:[/b] You can even use Armored trains (including the legendary Saviour of Karelia) or Railroad artillery installations that are rare guests in digital wargames. 

[b]4)[/b] (hi)story-driven gameplay
[b]Example:[/b] Lots of primary and secondary objectives with in-game dialogue by historical figures. Completing certain objectives provides unique global bonuses or trophies.

[b]5)[/b] Classical wargame with modern 3D graphics created with Unreal Engine 4.
[b]Example:[/b] You can see close up shots of tanks and other units moving with real physics across uneven terrain and enjoy the realistic 3D unit models instead of the usual counters.

[b]6)[/b] You can gain Heroes throughout the campaign and assign them to chosen units. All heroes are historical figures and allow units to get special powerful skills.
[b]Example:[/b] The deadliest sniper in WW2 history - Simo Häyhä - will join your troops
With 542 confirmed kills, and an unconfirmed total number of 705, not only was Simo Häyhä the deadliest sniper of World War II, but perhaps the deadliest sniper of all time. His nickname “the White Death” was well-earned.

[b]7)[/b] Different victory types, awards and ranks. You get different victory types based on your performance throughout the operations. That determines what awards you get and when you will be promoted to the next rank. 
[b]Example:[/b] All awards and ranks are not just an insignia, but provide gameplay bonuses - higher ranks means more Command points, while awards also provide discounts for units and make the HQ unit stronger.

[b]8)[/b] Cinematics - around 70 minutes in each title 
[b]Example:[/b] Before and after every operation you watch a cinematics sequence with historical characters delving deeper into the events of WW2 and the historical flow.

[b]9)[/b] Advanced supply system - great depth with little micromanagement
[b]Example:[/b] There are different types of Infrastructure across the map. Supply points transport the supplies across the map. If you break the supply chain by damaging, capturing or cutting off (blocking with ZoC) its elements - the enemy troops will be left without supplies.

[b]10)[/b] Both historical (75%) and alternate history (25%) operations.
[b]Example:[/b] You can enjoy both real historical battles and explore “what if” outcomes based on real plans and were never realised, like Sea Lion, or Operation Unthinkable. 

[b]11)[/b] Improved combat system - lethal vs nonlethal damage, 4 levels of spotting, various skills and equipment, significance of terrain, LoS and ZoC, different weather conditions and nighttime. 
[b]Example:[/b] The tactical moves feel quite diverse thanks to the original Panzer General mechanics that went through a very significant rework and upgrade. 

[b]12)[/b] Advanced transportation system - ground transport (trucks and APCs), train, aircraft or ship transportation. 
[b]Example:[/b] All ground units can be assigned truck or APC they board if they have to move far - at the same time they are vulnerable while in transit. Additionally, you can board trains, ships and aircraft for large distance troops transfer and landing operations. 

[b]13)[/b] All types of units can get special equipment, allowing you to finetune your troops to better tackle the task at hand.
[b]Example:[/b] Units can get diverse equipment such as: flamethowers, sappers squad, mortars, recoilless rifles, smoke generators, torpedoes, incendiary shells, or even dummy tanks.  

[b]14)[/b] Upgrade units to newer models to carry over crew’s experience. Out of line upgrades are more expensive. 
[b]Example:[/b] Upgrading Pz IV C to Pz IV F is much cheaper than replacing it with a Tiger II.

[b]15)[/b] Advanced naval combat system - all ships have parts such as all sorts of armament, hull, engine, flight deck, etc. with their own HP and functionality that deteriorates as they are getting damaged.
[b]Example:[/b] Ship has extra defense when its Engine part is operational. When the engine is damaged the ship loses its movement points and the extra defense it had due to mobility. Same with all types of guns etc. The maintenance team repairs the ship overtime, but you could also use the emergency repair team in case your ship is in dire straits.

[b]16)[/b] You can play some of the enemy units as well, if you manage to capture them during the battles.
[b]Example:[/b] In Spirit of Liberty Finns can get their hands on Russian BT--7s, T-34s, KV-1s, ISU-152 and other cool stuff.

[b]17)[/b] All units gain experience and can learn additional skills every time they level up.
[b]Example:[/b] Infantry can get a Forced march level up skill allowing it to move 2 extra Move points 3 times per operation. Artillery can learn to move 1 tile after firing to quickly change its position etc. 

Looking forward to discussing the community survey results with you
Starni Games team

notes.title: Weekly Intelligence Report #31
notes.content:
General! Our ever-vigilant intelligence service has prepared a news update, for your eyes only!
Here are all of our spy’s key findings.

[h2]SM: Fight for Freedom release. First results[/h2]

The Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom was released 10 days ago. While it is too early to judge, we can already see the first sales results, and they are quite discouraging. We will give you a more detailed report in the next Dev Diaries issue, but so far the release was underwhelming despite our best efforts to promote the game. It seems that this time we got much less traffic from Steam, despite decent day 1 sales compared to previous titles. The game was not featured in the “New and trending” tab (unlike all the previous titles). Technically it was, but only very briefly. So, we will gather all the data and explain all of it in Dev Diaries.

At the same time, we are happy that despite the low number of players - those of you who did find the game, left mostly positive feedback. So, we are happy that most players enjoy the game and find it of good quality. It is very important for us to know your opinion. There are not many reviews for now, which makes sense looking at the sales numbers, but most of them are positive, and we hope to keep that trend, by addressing all existing issues in a timely manner.

[h2]Issues with cinematics (already fixed)[/h2]

Many of you could have noticed that during the first week there were some issues with cinematics video and sound. The truth is that we could not finish and polish them properly before the planned release date, and we did not want to reschedule it, so we were trying to finish them in time for the release. Unfortunately, some of them were added last minute and there was literally no time to correct the sound for them. By next Friday we sorted out all these shortcomings. 

We are sorry for these issues, and will make sure to have better planning next time and have everything ready well in advance. There were some force majeure factors at play this time, like one of our 3D artists breaking right hand and being out of commission for about 2 months and other problems. We will tell you about it in more detail in Dev Diaries, so stay tuned. Nonetheless, we totally understand that the players should always receive the final and polished product, and no force majeure factors should affect that. That is why we will take a more measured approach next time, which will probably delay the release, but ensure that everything is in order. 

[h2]New Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom videos on YouTube[/h2]

We keep an eye on all new videos on YouTube that feature Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom. We can recommend these two channels as they seem to have done quite a good overview of the game. We will keep you informed of the new high-quality YouTube coverage of the game.

notes.title: Update 3.08. Strategic Mind Anniversary 🛠
notes.content:
Admiral! Two years have passed since the Strategic Mind series began with an Early Access for the Strategic Mind: The Pacific on 30 April 2019. It has been a magnificent two years full of events and new releases. We would like to celebrate the Strategic Mind second anniversary - and what better way to celebrate there is, other than deliver a new update? 😉

The majority of the changes were based on the feedback and reports of the community - so we could not have done it without you. We will keep improving the series and with your help, we can deliver much better results and turn the series into every wargamer’s dream. We will keep looking for your feedback and suggestions and continue to develop the series.

So, here we are with all the hottest fixes and features from the upcoming Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom.

[h2]Update 3.08[/h2]

[h3]New content:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fully reworked naval combat tutorial - now it consists of 3 parts. 
[*] Overhauled 5-parts of the land operations tutorial, but the content is the same.
[*] All tutorial operations now work much better. It was hard to click certain hexes/units in tutorials before, and now these issues were fixed. [/list]
[h3]Game mechanic changes: [/h3]
[list][*] Overwatch fire now does take into account Line of sight. (Before it was only Spotting and Gun range). So, now the anti-tank guns can no longer Overwatch you “through” the building, city or forest, etc. They can only Overwatch you where they would have been able to fire normally.   
[/list]
[h3]Quality of life improvements:[/h3]
[list][*] Added special “+” Overstrength indicator showing when each unit is eligible for an Overstrength.
[*] The terrain info screen now has two additional pieces of information: Line of Fire (Yes/No) and Combat penalty (Yes/No). 
[*] Added a “New hero available” notification when you get a new hero. You will see a flying label (similar to the “Level up available” one).
[*] Added hint to unit price when purchasing units with all the discount information so now you can see more clearly how different global bonuses, awards, and other things affect the final unit price. [/list]
[h3]Changes:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Infantry with Heavy equipment and no ground transport now cannot be deployed. (As it cannot move) The corresponding message box with an explanation is added. 
[*] Changed prices for Anti-aircraft guns equipment: Small searchlight now costs 10 Prestige, Medium searchlight - 20, Heavy searchlight - 30, Radar - 50.
[*] Fixed issue when boarding of the ground transport would not be displayed in a hex if there is enemy infrastructure. 
[*] Now, when the unit has no series, the “Series: none” is displayed.
[*] Moved the “Pause after every line” option was moved from Game Settings to Sound Settings.[/list]
[h3]Fixes:[/h3]
[list][*] Fixed the replenishment of equipment charges not working properly in some cases. Now you always get the charges replenished in the Service zone if you are eligible (Have the supply). 
[*] Fixed exploit with Undo button: you can no longer use Undo after changing the unit’s equipment. 
[*] Fixed exploit with Undo button: you can no longer gain extra movement by Using Undo after Close combat movement. 
[*] Fixed crash with Undo button during landing or take off - now it is unavailable after these actions.
[*] Fixed a rare issue that would lead to incorrect Line of Fire calculation in some cases.  
[*] Fixed an annoying sound that often happened during the loading screens. 
[/list]
[h3]Misc:[/h3]
[list][*] Corrected the Close quarters flying label “close defense” -> “close quarters” in all languages. 
[/list]

[h2]This is not the end[/h2]

You can now subscribe to our newsletter to gain unique wallpapers dedicated to the Strategic Mind series. You will also receive letters from us with unique content and some inside information. 

✉ [url=https://mailchi.mp/starnigames.com/game-menu]Subscribe to newsletter.[/url]

Looking forward to more feedback.

notes.title: Units in Fight for Freedom #16: US strategic bombers
notes.content:
Carpet bombings make for some of the most striking images of the Second World War - there’s a reason why the sight of leveled cities was often described as “moonscape”. Not many planes were capable of bringing such destructive power across such great distances - and the United States Air Force had an entire series of them.

[h2]B-17[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/e07bbbf2ab5ab73fe9a767f2f19d6a0f08a85535.jpg[/img]

The legendary B-17 “Flying Fortress” was a sturdy and reliable machine. Its payload was respectable, and its overall performance sufficed for hundreds of bombing raids across the entire Germany. The largest raid ever conducted by the Americans on Berlin consisted mostly of B-17s - and their combined might was horrifying.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/f68c5d7f62b9d703b3ab379103b10fd2016c1279.jpg[/img]

[h2]B-29[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/eecc48cf2cc636514d5777838424bcc18e23be23.jpg[/img]

Then, B-29 came around, dubbed “Superfortress” - its payload was 9000 kg. They wrought havoc across the Pacific, including the firebombing of Tokyo, and the nuclear detonations over Hiroshima and Nagasaki - the three most destructive air raids in the history of mankind.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/8effe5dd14ab245fc9e96e07c494f66810243ec0.jpg[/img]

[h2]B-36[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/d0c3f0f8493caaa53969fd65ab20a9845d3026e5.jpg[/img]

B-36 was slated to become their successor, improved in every regard, but by 1946, it was too little, too late. Although, it is not too late for them in Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom, as we have an alternate history ending in 1946, allowing you to use B-36 in battle. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/edcb91a118cc1f68cd4d7f6ca977ba74151f1400.jpg[/img]

[h2]Strategic bombers in Fight for Freedom[/h2]

In the US campaign, for the first time in the Strategic Mind series, the player would have the 
option to acquire Strategic bombers as core units. All three units: B-17, B-29, and B-36 will be available for upgrades as one series, which makes upgrades cheaper. They will have passive ability Overwatch breakthrough (similar to that of the fighters, but no need to activate it). Another unique skill is Strategic bomber, that allows the flying fortresses to deal extra damage to infrastructure and reduce the ammo and fuel of the enemy units by destroying their supplies. On top of that their combat parameters, especially defense, will be quite high. All this glory comes at a hefty cost though, both for the acquisition and repair.

notes.title: Map creation process in Strategic Mind: from an idea to a game-ready scenario
notes.content:
Hello, guys! Today we will tell you in detail about the whole scenario creation process. To illustrate it we will use footage taken during the creation of the 5th scenario of the US campaign in the upcoming Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom — Western Allied invasion of Germany. 

The following article is brought to you by [url=https://www.facebook.com/alex.marchenko.58]Alex Marchenko[/url], Lead Level Designer at Starni Games.

[h2]Stage 1: Creating a PSD file[/h2]

Every level development starts with the Narrative Designers making research about a chosen operation. After studying different maps of the region (war plans, geographic maps, river maps etc.), they are making a PSD file with all hexes, where terrain types are marked with different colors.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/a177b28654760792e2456b0bd4ce3e3ce8474bc6.png[/img]
[i]- Terrain design in a PSD file.[/i]

After designing the terrain, the Narrative Designers put different symbols on separate layers indicating: roads, infrastructure, units, objectives and other tips for the Level Designers team.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/0ca53548ff23e6b562cc4eb940befb482fcfcffa.png[/img]
[i]- PSD file with all the marks. Well, almost all.[/i]

Additionally, Narrative Designers create a larger version of the map that includes territories outside the combat zone — hex grid, but which are still visible. We do not want our maps to be cut off abruptly at the edge, so we put considerable extra effort to create additional terrain around the operational area to allow a gradual fade of the visible area into the fog.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/40798b62144e211c48a4b2f3d222bff4e01f2570.png[/img]
[i]- Full level. Play Zone (operational area) is marked by the red rectangle.[/i]

[h2]Stage 2: Importing a PSD file to Unreal Engine. Heightmap creation and import[/h2]

Now Level Designers make an empty level in Unreal Engine, using a sample with pre-set world settings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/438913e2038f0ec8d2240a7aed7c20c4cc964791.png[/img]
[i] - An empty level in UE4.[/i]

Next, the Level Designers use an automated script written by our Programmers to import the hex grid and all technical parameters of hexes, such as terrain types, roads and infrastructure locations into Unreal Engine 4. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/b25510945643961753edb2eace11e6fda52fe85b.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/78b489409b26a41a4a4d754081760a7afed5fd97.png[/img]
[i]- A level with imported data: terrain types, roads, railroads, rivers, deployment hexes, etc.[/i]

Using Photoshop, Level Designers make a Heightmap of the level. The Heightmap is a special file that indicates the landscape heights at different areas of the map.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/6a5de6471c6ea3455c3bd02f6be4a44a43bef03a.png[/img]
[i]- This is how the Heightmap file looks in Photoshop.[/i]

The Heightmap is then imported into UE4 as well, using the engine's features.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/19f4fe2f2cc2bdff0571996b32369a2bbe7ca229.png[/img]
[i]- The map after the heightmap file import.[/i]

[h2]Stage 3: Adding the terrain color and texture[/h2]

Next step is coloring the landscape according to different terrain types. First, the Level Designers create masks for all kinds of terrain in Photoshop.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/6cd2413a2d442799d8b69a1d13e48cca141b5e5d.png[/img]
[i]- Terrain masks for the level.[/i]

Next, we import masks into the engine, using UE4 features. As you may know, we have different visual types of maps, such as “Europe”, “Africa”, “Winter”, “Steppe”, and “Pacific”. We have also added “Jungles” setup in SM: Fight for Freedom for the operation in Burma.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/f146530c6860e01abf0112c0f8a0cd47d22894fa.jpg[/img]
[i]- This is how the level looks in the editor after adding terrain colouring and textures.[/i]

[h2]Stage 4: Creating water surfaces [/h2]

The next step is to create big rivers and lakes on the level, using UE4 tools such as splines and planes (not the fighter planes ;) ). After that, we have to smooth the river banks and paint it in the “sand” and “ground” terrain for better looks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/c6f9e7e64fc18d1c4efc59366510f1a888ce9969.png[/img]
[i]- The level with the proper river.[/i]

[h2]Stage 5: Laying roads, railroads and small rivers — a hell on earth[/h2]

It is now time for the hardest part of level creation — laying roads, railroads and small rivers. Why is it so hard? Well, the UE4 splines are “a pain in the ... arm”, as our Level Designers would say. The task here is to lay splines on the landscape so that none will float in the air or fall through the terrain. There are useful tools to help you achieve that, but it still requires a considerable amount of manual work. Also rivers should always go downhill, so hills and mountains on their way are a regular problem. Nevertheless, a job is a job, so here is the level after road and river management:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/2146acedf322a5f8c82051700cfa614c3ec9bd23.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/ca9201cc858c4226a574ce123277732986c46545.jpg[/img]
[i]- The level has roads, railroads and small rivers, but no cities, bridges etc.[/i]

Well, the hardest part of the work is now finished.

[h2]Stage 6: Adding buildings and infrastructure[/h2]

Next step is to put buildings on the level: bridges over big and small rivers, houses in the city hexes, and infrastructure: supply points/hubs, airfields, ports, and railway stations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/6f50263691da2dd3e7c5a4af691d90aef49e73dd.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/fc1a5c8ae91634430e1b2db8da1f23d79bc2dc91.jpg[/img]
[i]- The roads no longer look weird — we have bridges and houses. [/i]

[h2]Stage 7: Planting trees, flowers, stones and adding birds. Adding more visual polish[/h2]

Now it is time to give the nature some respect – we plant trees and flowers, throw stones, and raise birds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/878304176b35b60bcc5d6536a9e1be03d94a6679.png[/img]
[i]- At this point, the work on the visual components is pretty much done.[/i]

It is high time to give some additional personalization to the level by putting different environmental features, such as destructible assets: wooden fences, statues, electric poles etc. We also add animated objects, using UE4 blueprints, such as: spinning windmills, spotlights, lighthouses etc.

We also add some of the iconic buildings and geographical features like Stonehenge, Kremlin, the Great Barrier Reef etc. 

Last cosmetic part would be painting the river bottom with rocks and sea shallow water with seashells, adding clouds in the sky and putting a fog box around the map so that players cannot see “the edge of the world”. 

[h2]Stage 8: Placing units and their equipment[/h2]

Now we have to place the enemy units on map, including fortifications, such as forts and minefields, giving them suitable equipment and vehicles. Then we will place the player-controlled non-core units. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/6a468325bd4c3e7381f9419dc0003b0604b92612.png[/img]
[i]- Units that are still without models are marked as question marks.[/i]

[h2]Stage 9: Writing mission scripts[/h2]

The last part would be writing scripts and finally testing it over and over again, until perfect balance is achieved.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/6ce27d2d9d29b3290ae4e37aea63ededeb6613f2.png[/img]
[i]- This is how the operation script files look like. It is the Saar offensive script.[/i]

At first we just test the scripts and fix obvious balance issues for a single scenario. At this stage the use of cheat codes is allowed to speed up the testing. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/078df935ea5628c169d6c147551409bc4a612105.png[/img]
[i]- The first tests of the operation.[/i]

As you can see, the player units have 99 strength. Also there is no localisation for mission names and no pictures for the units at the bottom of the screen. Some units don't even have a model and only have a placeholder “question mark” model instead.

[h2]Stage 10: Campaign playthrough — a more thorough testing of all operations[/h2]

At this stage several people on the team have to do a full campaign playthrough, testing all scenarios in a consecutive manner and without any unfair advantages — they play exactly as the players would, to gauge the difficulty and adjust all the rough edges. Of course having played Strategic Mind games a lot, they have a very good understanding of the game, so we have to take that into account when setting the turn limits and balancing enemy units.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/09b172ebb6d68aaa26d1ae7e5739d4be1721feb1.png[/img]
[i]- The UK campaign first full playthrough completed. Some of the awards pictures are still in development.[/i]

[h2]Closing words[/h2]

The process of map creation from the “Basic idea is created” to the “Game ready” stage usually takes about 2 weeks. Enormous maps such as the Battle of Moscow in SM: Blitzkrieg may take up to 4 weeks. Each map requires the work of at least 4 different specialists: narrative designer creating texts and concept, level designer creating visuals, technical level designer writing scripts and QA specialist looking for bugs.

[h3]P. S. [/h3]

[b]Bonus screenshot:[/b] that’s how we test maps before our artists finished working on all the unit models.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/a50ae7300b27378073c6d7c9ba3fadcceae1b9d5.png[/img]
[i]- Just imagine how difficult it is to wage war while all your troops are just a bunch of marks with different stats, lying around across the battlefield.[/i]

Share your thoughts in the comments below!

If you want to support our efforts - wishlist and follow our upcoming title:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1381850/Strategic_Mind_Fight_for_Freedom/

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1381850/Strategic_Mind_Fight_for_Freedom/][img]https://media.giphy.com/media/1bazbW7RshUKHbrj45/giphy.gif[/img][/url]

With best regards
Starni Games team

notes.title: Starni Games 2020 report
notes.content:
Hello, guys! There are many opinions about the year 2020. Many think it was a bad and troublesome year. Some think 2021 will be even worse. We do not think, we make games. So, we will tell you about all the events happening with Starni Games in 2020, and let you make your own conclusions.

[h2]Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg release[/h2]
We have started to work on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1200330/Strategic_Mind_Blitzkrieg/]Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg[/url] back in 2019, right after [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/991810/Strategic_Mind_The_Pacific/]The Pacific[/url] release. Yet the majority of the work was done in 2020. It was tough to meet the deadliner, but we did it despite all the troubles. The release was a success, and the game is doing reasonably well. 

[h2]Big Battle: pandemic vs release [/h2]
We had to work remotely in April and May 2020, just before the Blitzkrieg release. Then we got back to the office, but in October went remote again for a month. Overall, working remotely and doing Mocap and VO mid-pandemic was quite challenging. If you want to know more about it [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1200330/announcements/detail/2933496588880999763]make sure to check out our Developer’s Diaries dedicated to these issues[/url].

[h2]Russian government stops the Blitzkrieg[/h2]
Soon after the Blitzkrieg release, the Russian government demanded that Steam remove it from the store in Russia. Moreover, the spokesman of the Russian president commented on it. They even claimed to file an official investigation request to the UN. If you want to find out more about the issue, [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1200330/announcements/detail/2247806424014858209]make sure to check our news about it[/url].

[h2]Free game Demo[/h2]
This year we started to create free Demo versions for our games, to make sure you can try them out before buying. We want to make sure that you know what you get.

👉[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1381850/Strategic_Mind_Fight_for_Freedom/]Check out our latest Demo here[/url].

However, at first, there were issues. When we submitted the Blitzkrieg Demo 3 months after we published the game, Steam blocked both the full game and the Demo. We had to start all the explanations anew. We managed to lift the limitation off of the full game, but only at the cost of creating a German-only version with Hitler’s face blurred. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1200330/announcements/detail/2885076552142109470]You can learn more about it here[/url]. 

[h2]Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism release[/h2]
All the while we kept working on the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1341170/Strategic_Mind_Spectre_of_Communism/]Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism[/url]. The release date was planned for 13 November, and once again we had to work remotely for some time and faced some other problems. All in all, we managed to break through the enemy’s encirclement and released the game on time. It was our most polished and smooth release so far. 

[h2]Hitler is more popular than Stalin[/h2]
Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism release was the least successful to date in financial terms, but the game got the highest review score so far. It sold 2 times fewer copies than Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg. However, due to other projects still showing decent results we are able to continue with the Strategic Mind series. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1200330/announcements/detail/2933497222873336045]We discuss it in more detail here[/url]. 

[h2]New Starni Games website and Starni Store[/h2]
Just on the last day of the year, we managed to release our new website - starnigames.com. The design was fully reworked. It will get further polish in January. You can also buy our games (Steam keys) there directly from the developer. Yet, if you prefer to do it on steam - we are more than happy with that. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1200330/announcements/detail/2934623681424828503]You can learn more about the website and different stores here[/url]. 

[h2]Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom - the work has begun[/h2]
In November and December, we were working really hard and made good progress, making a full release of our next title in Q2 2021 very realistic. So, far [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wWvKdLDLbh8]we have the first gameplay trailer[/url] and an early Free Demo with the first operation. We plan to update the Demo as our work progresses and release more trailers along the way. We will keep you updated on our progress through regular news and Developer’s Diaries. 

[h2]Developers Diaries[/h2]
This year we started to issue Developer’s Diaries regularly and plan to keep doing so in 2021, so stay tuned. In case you missed our story so far, you can check it out here:
1. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1200330/announcements/detail/2746585154891303969]New VO and mocap setup[/url]
2. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1200330/announcements/detail/5382318210069094881]Units’ speech review. Part 1[/url]
3. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1200330/announcements/detail/2901962512557554806]Units’ speech review. Part 2[/url]
4. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1200330/announcements/detail/2941374083279593000]Strategic Mind Franchise Soundtrack[/url]
5. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1200330/announcements/detail/2943626518457443398]Undo feature, new music, and hilarious moments[/url]
6. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1200330/announcements/detail/2926738653835865509]Designing winter operations[/url]
7. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1200330/announcements/detail/2910976689287963848]5 days after the release, new ice visuals[/url]
8. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1200330/announcements/detail/2933496588880999763]A windy road[/url]
9. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1200330/announcements/detail/2933497222873336045]Communist Economy[/url]

[h2]Developer’s Gameplay[/h2]
We also started a series of Developer’s Gameplay, where our Lead Game Designer plays our games with commentary, telling you more about the game mechanics and the development process. 

[previewyoutube=out9Rh8xRvQ;full][/previewyoutube]
New episodes will be available in January 2021, so stay tuned. We want to be even more open and transparent about our production, so feel free to ask any questions you like and we will do our best to answer them in future episodes.

notes.title: Developers' Diaries #8
notes.content:
Hello, guys! After the launch of Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism last month, we can finally tell you a bit more about the whole process. Recently, many companies started to attribute various delays and issues to the pandemics. We will do another thing: tell you how we managed to release the game on time, despite a number of setbacks along the road. 

[h2]Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg release[/h2]
The lockdown reached Kyiv in early April. We were working from the office up until the subway and other public transport ceased to function. Then we set up remote work tools and started working from home.

One of the issues was that part of Halder’s VO was unfinished, the actor doing his part lived in another city, and all trains between our cities were canceled. So, we had to ask him to record remotely and the sound was different from our usual setup.

Working from home was quite challenging, especially for people on the team who have children asking their Papa to “play with them, not do some stupid work”. So, our CEO and Lead Programmer at once Ihor Tymoshenko kept working from the office all along during this time to avoid family distractions and focus on the work.

Other people had troubles with working hours - at home, you just sleep, eat, and work, there is no boundary between “workplace” and “home”, especially prior to release. Yet we have managed to overcome all of these issues and deliver the game on schedule. 

[h2]Back to office[/h2]
The release of the Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg on 22 May coincided with public transport being available again, so on the 25th of May, we again started to work from the office. It is really convenient in terms of communication and coordination of actions. It does consume some time to get to the office, but at least you have some boundaries between work and home environments. Also, there is no better time to think about the project than on your way to the office, or back home. 

[h2]New challenges[/h2]
Getting back to the office was far from the end of our adventures. Working together meant following all the safety procedures, like wearing masks in public places and transport, making sure to use antiseptics, etc. We still follow all the rules and try to do whatever we can to minimize the risk of catching a virus or spreading it to our colleagues. That worked well enough throughout the summer. 

[h2]Autumn comes, people get ill[/h2]
In October one of the guys on our team caught the virus, so we immediately offered all the team to work remotely until things settle. Several other people on the team have also gotten ill but with some regular illnesses, and our marketing manager even had to go through an appendectomy. All of that came at about the same time, which was highly unfortunate. 

Additionally, the person in charge of the VO organization and supervision got ill right during the VO period. Fortunately, this was not COVID, but it was one more setback for our VO production.

Later, the actress doing the female units voices also got ill, so we had to record a week before release in the end. Fortunately, all the cinematics VO sessions were finished during the summer.

[h2]By the skin of our teeth[/h2]
By the end of October, we finally got back to the office, and fortunately had no more serious illnesses on the team. Yet, the time was short, and making all the recently recorded VO game-ready, delivering all localizations and lots of other things was really hard to do in time for the planned 13 November release. We were able to provide the press with early access to the game only 5 days before the release, which is certainly not enough. Yet, during the release itself, we managed to deliver all the core content. Overall, we are happy with the result and that we were able to keep our promise and deliver a solid game on time. 

[h2]Better quality at Spectre of Communism release[/h2]
Despite all the adversities, Spectre of Communism was running quite smoothly at release. While there were some issues, and some minor problems are still getting fixed, judging by your feedback and by the amount of post-release patches, it seems that the game was much more solid at release this time around. There seem to be many more problems during the Blitzkrieg launch. We quickly addressed those issues, and are thankful to you for supporting us and reporting all the problems, allowing us to timely fix them. 

[h2]The work continues[/h2]
We have fixed most of the issues you have reported in Spectre of Communism, and have already started working on the upcoming Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom title, which is scheduled for Q2 2020. We keep working from the office, however, the situation in Ukraine has deteriorated threateningly over the course of autumn, and there are talks about some form of lockdown in January. So, we consider the possibility of going remote once again for some time, if such need arises. 

[h2]Financial results[/h2]
In the next issue of Developers’ Diaries, we will share some insights into the sales of Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism.

Stay tuned for more Developers’ Diaries next week.

[b]Support our team by adding the next project to your wishlist:[/b]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1381850/Strategic_Mind_Fight_for_Freedom/
With best regards
Starni Games team

notes.title: New units in Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism #10
notes.content:
[h1]Ilyushin Il-4 (DB-3F)[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/24e8772cb41f0ea3593af5b2cd29373bb150385b.png[/img]

A modification of earlier DB-3 bomber models. Despite being far from the best design as of 1941, these long-range bombers did perform several daring raids on Berlin in the summer of 1941, proving to Germans that their homeland could also suffer from war. Overall, more than 6000 planes of different modifications were built.

[h1]Petlyakov Pe-2[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/e9876bb4514b9817a2ccab1463e298366f2a069c.png[/img]

A twin-engined Soviet dive bomber, Pe-2 is considered one of the best aircraft models the USSR produced during the war. Its production numbers went over 11 000 units built.

The Pe-2 was designed in a prison design bureau (sharashka); Vladimir Petlyakov (head engineer) had been arrested and imprisoned in 1937 for allegedly delaying design work on the Tupolev ANT-42 bomber. Petlyakov was given the task of designing a high-altitude fighter, which he successfully accomplished. However, operational experience in the Soviet-Finnish War of 1939-1940 showed that this was not what the Soviet Air Force needed, and Lavrentiy Beria, head of the NKVD and of the sharashka system, ordered that the fighter be redesigned as a dive bomber, with the promise that Petlyakov and his colleagues would be released on its successful completion. The resulting aircraft, the Pe-2 proved to be one of the most successful designs of World War II.

Petlyakov was released in 1940, and was awarded a Stalin Prize in 1941. However, at Kazan, Petlyakov faced increasing difficulties, with many of his trained technicians and machinists conscripted into the Soviet military and sent to the front lines, which adversely affected the aircraft production. He protested to Soviet senior leadership, and was on his way to Moscow in January 1942 (flying in a Pe-2), when he died in an air crash near Arzamas.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/e30c4730ed0701406fa4b918d3dd56be7988848e.png[/img]

We will keep posting new units that will appear for the first time in the Strategic Mind series, so stay tuned!

With best regards

Hello guys!

With only one day left before the release, we would like to tell you more about the winter operations in the upcoming Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism. 

[h2]Where it all started[/h2]
In Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg we had the German drive towards Moscow. However, it was set in November and at first, there were heavy rains, then Rasputitsa followed, and only later the Frost would set in freezing all the rounds and solving the issue of Rasputitsa. At the same time, it was only the first snow, which melted quickly and would not result in thick snow until later into the winter. All other operations were spring to autumn. 

[h2]Winter is coming![/h2]
In the upcoming Spectre of Communism title, we added a number of winter operations, including the Battle of Moscow set in December 1941, where you have to make sure the Germans do not end up storming the Kremlin. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/890886e2b0e24efc449c879dce91072b4834482f.jpg[/img]

[h2]The Winter War [/h2]
The toughest winter operation is probably the Winter War against Finland. Only here, Frost effect changes to a Severe frost, which applies penalty even for units with Winter equipment. While units without the winterized equipment have their movement points reduced to a maximum of 1 on top of other penalties. So, it is crucial to supply all of your ket units with proper equipment in this operation and be ready that Severe frost will slow down the latter part of the operation. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/2377a01470675150b3d6c707cb9a09e4e2217f45.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/64f17df6d99d1b5806285d48c30bf82452267a86.png[/img]

[h2]The Battle of Moscow[/h2]

It is not eligible if: an attack happened, the spotting has changed, the objective status has changed, the unit embarked/disembarked, etc.

[h2]Optimization [/h2]
We are working on optimizing the game performance. So, far we successfully implemented a number of improvements. Some are still underway and will be added in future updates, as we keep working on the Strategic Mind series.

This changelog is not an exhaustive list of changes, some minor improvements in other areas were also made, some bugs were fixed, and some localization inaccuracies corrected.

notes.title: 2 days left! New units in Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism part 7
notes.content:
[h2]BM-13 [/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38153924/19a20a6698b8604b149cae464736980b52cd401f.png[/img]

Katyusha multiple rocket launcher is a type of rocket artillery first built and fielded by the Soviet Union in World War II. It was a surprise for the Germans early into the war in 1941, however, they did not consider it a big threat. Only massive Katyusha fire, the USSR troops adopted in 1943 cand later, turned out to be the effective way to employ this weapon. 

The BM-13 model was usually mounted on top of the ZIS truck. 

[h2]BM-13N[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38153924/c48ef5bddccb0eb42bb7ba3dfb9bf1e7f27172f6.png[/img]

The improved BM-13N model was usually mounted on the US lend-lease Studebaker US6 trucks. There were other modifications, like BM 31, also on Studebaker chassis, but with larger caliber rockets. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38153924/b4935ab83f1aebdfedeb4de5933cfa58efdf0401.png[/img]

Katyusha MLRs have become a part of folklore, making popular the Russian song about a girl named Katyusha (Russian name). It was considered an instrumental weapon of Soviet victory. Although it’s precision left much to be desired, the massed Katyusha’s fire had, according to many accounts, a devastating effect on the German troops’ morale. 

In the game, Katyusha rocket launchers, have quite low attack values, but they can attack two times every turn and move 3 hexes away after each attack. Combined with high mobility, that makes Katyusha MLRs a very versatile tool. We had MB-13 in our previous titles, but we added two more models, adjusted their stats, and added special skills. So, now this is a much more potent instrument of war. 

We will keep posting new units that will appear for the first time in the Strategic Mind series, so stay tuned!

With best regards
Starni Games team

notes.title: Developers' Diaries #4
notes.content:
This summer we have released the Strategic Mind Franchise Soundtrack that will contain all the music for the Strategic Mind series (with the exception of the majority of The Pacific tracks), and all the money we gain from selling it is going into the creation of new tracks.

[h2]Why no The Pacific tracks?[/h2]
The issue with music in Strategic Mind: The Pacific is that we bought music with a 1 commercial product license, and it’s not unique. It may be great music and fit the game, but other projects can use it as well, and we can only use it in one product. There are only 4 tracks written by an individual composer that are available in the Strategic Mind Franchise Soundtrack. 

[h2]Why create our own music?[/h2]
After we realized the issue above, we found a group of composers united under the name of Daraba Studio, who are now in charge of composing and recording all the music for our projects. Starting from Blitzkrieg we own all commercial rights and therefore can release all tracks in a separate soundtrack etc. Additionally, we are always hard-pressed on budget, so creating a separate soundtrack is a great way to add more tracks into the game than originally planned. Finally, we have read a number of users’ requests for a soundtrack, and that is what finally tipped the balance in favor of this new approach. 

[h2]How is our progress so far?[/h2]
The community is quite supportive of the Soundtrack idea, and we thank you for that. So far, we have gathered enough funds from Soundtrack sales to order additional 3 tracks that will be added to the existing soundtrack along with all the Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism tracks that we created using our default budget. All community-funded tracks will have a [Community supported] tag in their name, so you could tell which tracks were added owing to your support.

[h2]What are our future plans?[/h2]
We hope that more players will buy the soundtrack during the Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism release, and it will help us create more Community supported tracks for the next project. If the soundtrack sales would exceed our expectations, we could create some additional tracks for Spectre of Communism and add them to the project when they are ready with one of the updates. 

[h2]Adding historical tracks[/h2]
In Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg we started experimenting with historical music. The problem with it is that there is no copyright on the old music composition (it expired), but there is copyright for the old music performance(recording). That means we have to record our own version of the old songs and music. We do not have the budget for the chorus, so we create only instrumentals. In Blitzkrieg we added 2 tracks to see how they fit the game:

Wenn die Soldaten:
[previewyoutube=Hxp07uxJic0;full][/previewyoutube]
White Army, Balck Baron (aka “The Red Army is the Strongest”):
[previewyoutube=DdzaN9lSasM;full][/previewyoutube]
We were satisfied with the result, so we decided to continue adding some percentage of the tracks of old times in the next titles.

[h2]Historical tracks in Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism[/h2]
Here is the Soviet Air Force March: 
[previewyoutube=g7EGetVNaX0;full][/previewyoutube] 
We also plan to add “The Internationale” and “Korobeiniki”. Additionally, one of the three community-supported tracks will be “Oh Fields, My Fields”. 

[h2]Cinematic tracks[/h2]
We also create special cinematic tracks, that are usually up to 1 minute long and are used only in cinematics. Here are some new cinematic tracks from Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism.

Zhukov theme:
[previewyoutube=bKhYShXu1vI;full][/previewyoutube]
Battle theme:
[previewyoutube=Yt546nKbkdk;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]Gameplay tracks[/h2]
Gameplay tracks are played at random during the actual gameplay. We will use the tracks from Blitzkrieg and the new tracks. Additionally, this time we want to try and use some of the historic tracks in the gameplay tracks capacity and are eager to hear your feedback.

[h2]Soundtrack update[/h2]
We will update the Strategic Mind Franchise Soundtrack on the Spectre of Communism release date so that all current and future owners will get access to new tracks as well. 

[h2]Your feedback and support[/h2]
Your feedback is very important to us. It is actually you who suggested creating a soundtrack as a separate entity, we just built on that idea. Your thoughts about music quality and its nature are invaluable to us, so make sure you do share your thoughts on our community hubs and in the comments below. Also, every soundtrack purchase makes us one step closer to adding yet another track into the series. So, we greatly appreciate your support.

We will post the next issue of the Developers’ Diaries as soon as we can, so stay tuned. 

With best regards
Starni Games team

Since Panzer Strategy development we wanted to add unit lines — some things units will say at random commenting on the in-game events.

[h2]We strive for diversity[/h2]

Every class of units had its own set of lines and triggers, like: selection, movement, attack, killing an enemy, forcing the enemy to retreat, low/out of ammo/fuel, enemy spotted, etc. Here are some of them:

[h2]Unique in everything![/h2]

Please, let us know what are your impressions and experience with the unit speech.

notes.title: Developers’ Diaries #1 by Starni Games
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/891ed0875e18d9564c6a5969679a7d4c61a55a6d.png[/img]

Hello guys!

Creating games is a challenging, creative and exciting process.

We decided to share with you what happens behind the scenes in our new series
of articles — Developers’ Diaries by Starni Games.

Recently, we have announced our next project Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism (to be released in Q4 2020). We are already working full steam on the project. 

Last week we tested a new setup for mocap and sound recording: we tested two different microphones to decide what is the best way to record sound and animation for Spectre of Communism. Additionally, we had to decide whether to switch to an adjusted production process for mocap and VO.

We tested two microphones: stationary studio mic and DPA microphone lavalier. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/63e121069e54d0f8f9c63e16a3ef2c2bbdf982ef.jpg[/img]

Microphone lavalier is used on TV and in TV-series if the actor has to move a lot during the recording as it is very convenient and moves with the actor.

Studio stationary mic is used for music recording, podcasts and radio. It is fixed in place and cannot be used by a moving actor.  

Despite the stationary mic providing finer details of the voice, we decided to use the lavalier mic as it offers high quality recording while also allows movement. It is extremely important for us as we will use the motion capture technologies to record the movements and facial animations of the actor and then transfer them to the game character. If we use a stationary mic, the sound will drop if the actor turns his head away from the mic to look at the other character. 

Our cinematic director Constantine tries out the some of the motion capture equipment setup:

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/UqwftHrCQlWx4TyDHK/giphy.gif[/img]

Our COO Oleksandr is adjusting the helmet with an attached Iphone, which is used to capture facial animations:

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/YoQqlob9pYhBTm9ApQ/giphy.gif[/img]

Some weird stuff happening during the tests. The good thing is that the issue was quickly solved:

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/MByYBtFz8FY1nGFuru/giphy.gif[/img]

[h3]The results of test[/h3]
We decided to go for a new technical setup.

[h3]Old production process[/h3]
Motion capture + preliminary VO made by one actor for all characters.
All other voice actors had to fit the preliminary VO and lip sync during the final VO. 

[h3]Planned production process[/h3]
Motion capture + final VO at the same time by every actor. We think this way the voice and animation will be a better match. The time will tell. 

We hope that these adjustments and new mic will help us deliver the cinematics of higher quality in the upcoming project.

The VO + mocap sessions will start soon. We will keep you informed about our progress. 

Your Starni Games team

We would like to congratulate the players’ community with the 2 months anniversary of Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg.

These two months we work hard to fix all of the reported issues and further improve the game: 18 updates in two months can truly be called “a Blitzkrieg” on its own.
[h3]What we have done[/h3]
Apart from bug fixes, the game went through the following improvements:
[list]
[*] New Equipment added + all equipment balancing 
[*] Balance changes for the majority of operations
[*] Steam achievements added:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36661203/bcd6442936692c02a9a0957b05ee2d9d6fa653d0.png[/img]
[*] Naval tutorial added
[*] Better Steam integration
[*] You can adjust difficulty after every operation
[*] Added new terrain type — Street, improving the city-combat part of the gameplay 
[*] Added option to set a delay after each phrase 0-5 sec
[*] All new save files are now archived, so they take tenfolds less disk space now
[*] Added option to set the number of last save files 10-100 — the rest will be deleted automatically
[*] Slight UI improvements etc.
[/list]
The majority of these changes were inspired by your feedback which we carefully accumulated and immediately acted upon. We look forward to more feedback from you guys!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36661203/05307cdc55f129234ba6067633d23ef4a7bfada0.png[/img]

The roadmap for the future updates is currently looking like that
[list]
[*] Leaderboards: recording your score and comparing it to the other players globally
[*] Steam Community Items: trading cards, badges etc.
[*] The “Undo” button: the ability to correct a misclick, if it did not result in a fight or spotting of the enemy unit.
[/list]
[h3]Strategic Mind: The Pacific update[/h3]
Another important matter is that most of the important changes were transferred to the Strategic Mind: The Pacific as well. So, all the players of Strategic Mind series can benefit from the improvements. This also means that when the next Strategic Mind title will come out, many important features will be added retrospectively to Strategic MInd: Blitzkrieg as well.

[h3]Upcoming project in Strategic Mind series[/h3]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1341170/Strategic_Mind_Spectre_of_Communism/

notes.content:

Today, a day before the release, we want to look back at the production process and compare Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg with Strategic Mind: The Pacific. Let us look into what key features and improvements were added in the second installment of the project.
Core content:
[list]

Many of these changes will be retrospectively added into Strategic Mind: The Pacific with the upcoming update.

notes.title: Players feedback inspired features in Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg
notes.content:
Since the Panzer Strategy release in 2018, we were gathering lots of valuable feedback from the players. Some things we could implement fast, for others we had to do extensive preliminary work. Thus, we always note what the players ask for and try to implement it as soon as we have the opportunity.  

Strategic Mind: The Pacific development allowed us to implement many (but not all) of the community suggestions both from Panzer Strategy and from The Pacific early access period. Among the new features, added due to your feedback were:
Detailed combat prediction window
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/054d49d2f678a08158ff2ad7030b9c00ab95d452.png[/img]
Many hints, explanations, and Manual (far from perfect, but a good start)
Terrain and infrastructure info
Naval combat tutorial
Further camera zoom option.
Units speech, zoom-in on unit renders, and others.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/9f8d6b45ca9c7cbdb3e73230cf73c7a8e48a2849.png[/img]
However, there were still more things that we wanted to implement but they required more time and preparations. So, we got some of them ready for the Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg release, namely:
You can now rename your units with custom names. (and the save files)
You can two choose between two sets of Controls: Modern (new) and Legacy (old). 
Modern (Unit selection - Left mouse button, Attack/Movement - Right mouse button, Open unit info screen - Middle mouse button (or I hotkey, or left-click on corresponding UI button))
Legacy (Unit selection - Left mouse button, Attack/Movement - Left mouse button, Open unit info screen - Right mouse button (or I hotkey, or left-click on corresponding UI button))
Added detailed 5-part tutorial for land operations
UI polish and improvements


Added calendar button indication Day/Night cycle
You can turn on/off the hex grid not only in the Settings but also with the H hotkey.
Added a separate setting for unit speech volume.
Improved Manual UI (We will keep improving it further in the future)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/14c0d699e4779fbd4ed3d2e821e16383c0de0339.png[/img]

All these features were brought by a combination of you being interested in our games, actively sending us lots of feedback and great suggestions, and by our willingness to listen to the community and improve our games together. We will keep adding new features and polishing the existing ones. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/13798723daed29a474e25e265a7562f05fd9e205.png[/img]

There are still many features that we want to add, but up to now lacked the time and resources to implement. The top two things on our “to-do” list right now are the integration of Steam cloud saves and Steam achievements. No ETA on these, but we will surely add them as soon as we can. 

Do not forget to wishlist Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg to show us your interest in the project and stay tuned for more information about new content and game development progress.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1200330/Strategic_Mind_Blitzkrieg/

With best regards
Starni Games development team

notes.title: Update 2.06
notes.content:
In today’s update 2.06 we fix more issues reported by the community and improved German localization.

[b]Changes:[/b]
[list][*] Corrected all German “technical localization” (all the abilities, ship parts descriptions, etc.) There might still be some things to fix with the new version, which we will address in later updates, but over we expect the quality of localization to increase dramatically. Next, we will work on fixing German subtitles for cinematics. If you play the game with German localization on, please do let us know what you think about these fixes.
[*] We made some changes to the Australia deployment phase: now you have only 4 deploy hexes in each location, representing the fact that not the whole fleet was able to reach Australia in time. You can deploy the rest of your units in the second deploy phase before turn 2. Additionally, we moved some of the enemy forces further away to balance out the increase in the difficulty of the objective to cover the Army landing. 
[*] Adjusted the stats of Japanese Ground transports, as some of them were incorrect. Additionally, the USA Ground transport LVT-4 now adds 2 Soft attack and 1 Hard attack as it had guns mounted on it.
[*] Fixed an occasional tutorial issue when the player could not press the “Acquire” button (Reported by [b]ChiefCommander33[/b], and others). (It was quite hard to replicate, as it was not happening on any of the PCs in our office. Luckily, one of our friends has encountered it on her laptop and allowed us to borrow it for a few days. Even then it was hard to figure it out). 
[*] Fixed important crash (reported by[b] [CHN]Zephyr[/b]), which was happening after an Infantry unit spent all its movement points, then got new Ground transport, and it could still move on the transport causing a crash. Another variant of the same issue was crash after the Infantry with transport got overrun and was shown ineligible hexes to move to, and if the player chose to move there the game would crash.
[*] Fix an issue with Japanese campaign 05 operation (reported by [b]Nix[/b]), where completing objectives in a certain order would cause a crash.
[*] Fix an issue with Japanese campaign 05 operation, the objective to pursue the enemy fleet was working incorrectly.
[*] Fixed USA campaign 04 operation secondary objective to kill submarines not giving experience to your Destroyers as a part of the reward. (Reported by [b]Tim[/b])
[*] Fixed USA campaign 06 operation secondary objective to capture the place where Marines barracks were not giving experience to your Marines as a part of the reward. (Reported by [b]The Matrix has you![/b])
[*] Fixed Japan campaign 05 operation secondary objective to prevent Zero capture, the turn timer was going up instead of going down.
[*] Fixed a rare bug in Japanese campaign 08 operation, where you would fail secondary objective even if you captured oil storages. (Reported by [b]aramoor50[/b], thank you for the save files)
[*] Fixed some visual elements on the map (eg. railroad on bridges etc) on several maps. 
[*] Fixed incorrect text in Japanese campaign 06 operations the secondary objective “capture the airfield at Munda” -> “Hold the airfield at Munda”. (Reported by [b]Night_Phoenix[/b])
[*] Fixed dialogue when first attacking Tekketsu Kinotai in USA campaign operation 09. 
[*] In the Japanese campaign 06 operation we moved the completion of the main objective to hold all victory hexes one turn earlier so that you do not get a warning that you have the last turn before indecision penalty kicks in even though you did everything perfectly.[/list]

We would like to thank all of our community members who keep reporting all the occurring issues and help us to make the game better. We do appreciate your help. Additionally, we would like to thank Night Phoenix for his Lets play series covering the Japanese campaign, as it also helped us to identify and fix a couple of issues. 

We will keep improving and polishing the game. Our team wishes everyone good holidays. Stay tuned as there are some big announcements coming. 

With best regards
Starni Games development team
